name: AI Driver Behaviour
author: Kizi
description: How AI drivers race and drive: gap to other cars, making room, slides and spins, damage, pace. Every driver can race differently. Experimental.

options.label: Close racing: gap to other cars
options.description: The gap an AI car keeps to other cars (the game's value is 0.35). Smaller = closer racing, None = no gap kept. The same for every car.

options.label: Close racing: when they make room
options.description: How much of a car must be alongside an AI car (0 to 1, the game's value is 0.33) before the AI moves over. Higher = it reacts later and holds its line.

options.label: Close racing: drivers differ
options.description: Gives each driver their own value around "when they make room" (up to ±0.06, ±0.12 or ±0.18), plus their own attack distance and commitment to a pass. Fixed per driver. The gap is not changed.

options.label: Slides: steering correction
options.description: Scales the AI's steering gains to 75, 50 or 25 % and slows its steering smoothing. Weaker = slides are caught later.

options.label: Slides: traction control
options.description: Scales the AI's traction control to half or off. Less = more wheelspin on corner exit.

options.label: Slides: when they lift off
options.description: How far into a slide the AI starts lifting off the throttle (the game's value is 0.5). Higher = it keeps full throttle deeper into a slide.

options.label: Slides: when they lose the car
options.description: The slide angle at which the AI gives up and spins (the game's value is 23 degrees). Smaller = it spins sooner.

options.label: Damage: speed with a damaged car
options.description: How much a damaged AI car slows down for corners and braking. Pushing = half the game's slowdown, Flat out = a quarter. Both also raise the speed limit with a puncture.
